name: Commodore SS Group A SV (VN)
hook: The rules said Holden had to build 500 of these red V8 sedans to go racing, and it stopped at 302.
story: Picture Australia at the end of the 1980s. Holden and Ford fight every weekend on the racetrack. And the rules say a race car needs road-going twins. Group A wants 500 of them, sold to the public. So Holden's performance arm builds the VN SS Group A. It is a big family Commodore with a 5.0-litre V8. It gets fuel injection, special internals and a six-speed ZF gearbox. A body kit and a tall rear wing finish the job. Almost all of them wear one colour, a deep red called Durif. It goes on sale late in 1990. But the target never arrives. Only 302 are built. Some say the price was too steep. Others say the rules were changing. Either way, the racing body lets the car race anyway. And then the whole idea fades. Soon Australian touring cars no longer need road twins at all. So this red sedan is where the story ends. It was the last Holden built to make a race car legal.
description: The VN Commodore SS Group A SV was a limited-run sedan built by Holden Special Vehicles to homologate the VN Commodore for Group A touring car racing. Its 5.0-litre fuel-injected V8 made 215 kW and drove the rear wheels through a six-speed ZF manual. Group A asked for 500 road cars, but only 302 were made, and the racing authority allowed it to compete regardless. It is remembered as the last of Holden's homologation specials, and most were painted Durif Red.
